entities.label: Person
entities.summary: René Cogny was a French Général de corps d'armée, World War II and French Resistance veteran and survivor of Buchenwald and Mauthausen-Gusen concentration camps. He was a commander of the French forces in Tonkin during the First Indochina War, and notably during the Battle of Dien Bien Phu. His post-war private and legal conflict with superior General Henri Navarre became a public controversy. Known to his men as Le General Vitesse, and reputable for his military pomp, physical presence and skill with the press, Cogny was killed in the 1968 Ajaccio-Nice Caravelle crash in the Mediterranean near Nice.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a commander of French forces in Tonkin during the First Indochina War and a survivor of Buchenwald and Mauthausen-Gusen concentration camps, René Cogny's experiences significantly impacted his perspective on military strategy and human rights. His post-war conflict with General Henri Navarre led to a public controversy that highlighted the complexities of French colonialism.
